title: Anthropic prices at $83 per share, setting the company up for an IPO above $1 trillion
excerpt: Anthropic has set its IPO price at $83 per share, valuing the company at around $1.5 trillion for its listing on Thursday.
content_html:
By Stephen Council

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-18T23:54:35.543Z

Anthropic will officially go public on Thursday at $83 a share, the company announced on Wednesday. That's above the range it had previously provided.

The AI juggernaut is setting itself up for a vast fundraise in its initial public offering. At the price, Anthropic will rake in at least $79 billion from its IPO, plus an additional $26 billion through a concurrent deal with several tech giants.

The price values the company at around $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The company had estimated a price range of $70 to $78 during its investor road show.

Anthropic said in its announcement that it would sell 956 million shares of its common stock, more than previously expected. It has also offered the IPO's underwriters, a group of banks led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the option to buy an additional 147 million shares. Existing shareholders will also sell over 23 million shares in the listing.

The company plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

Choosing a listing price for an IPO is a high-wire act. A higher price means Anthropic will raise more cash to fund its extraordinarily expensive rush for computing power, though companies often try to underprice to juice demand on IPO day.

Anthropic's expected IPO valuation was a moving target. Earlier this fall, reports emerged that some investors and bankers eyed a $2 trillion total. Jitters in the stock market, plus decelerating revenue growth at Anthropic's last disclosure, pared back the expectations for the Claude-maker's IPO.

It's still a humongous total. Anthropic is only five years old. A group of seven ex-OpenAI employees founded it in early 2021. At $1.5 trillion, Anthropic would be worth more than each of Walmart, Samsung, and Exxon Mobil.

Although Anthropic is not profitable under standard accounting practices, its rapid growth has stunned investors. In the third quarter of 2025, it generated $1.4 billion in revenue. In the third quarter of this year, it generated $17 billion.

After the IPO, would-be investors in Anthropic will be watching the speed of its revenue growth, the margins on its computing expenses, and the capabilities of its new AI models. CEO Dario Amodei has pitched life sciences as a potential new source of growth following the company's success in coding, though the area remains unproven.

For long-standing investors and employees, an IPO will allow the earliest backers to see stunning multiples on their original investments. Anthropic's cofounders are set to become multibillionaires.

They won't be able to take their winnings immediately, though. Anthropic's IPO comes with a staggered lock-up period, with release dates in the months ahead that will allow more shares to be sold.

And after the original price setting, Anthropic is at the whims of the public markets. Many companies that IPO end up seeing their share price eventually dip below the initial level, even after an early pop.

SpaceX, which went public in June, provides the closest parallel to Anthropic in terms of size. It went public with a $135 share price and raised $85.7 billion in its offering, after the underwriters exercised their option to buy additional shares.
